newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gold Fields Namibia smelter shut for weeks.
newsitem.headline: Gold Fields Namibia smelter shut for weeks.

text.p: Gold Fields Namibia Ltd said on Thursday that the copper smelter at its subsidiary Tsumeb Corp Ltd (TCL) could be closed for six weeks or longer through damage caused by striking workers.
"It could be six weeks, it could be even longer," Gold Fields spokesman Dermot Whyte told Reuters.
"All our operations are at a standstill at the moment," he added.
The company said the smelter at TCL had been badly damaged through action by striking members of the Mineworkers Union of Namibia who downed tools eight days ago.
On Thursday, the strike at TCL remained in force and strikers continue to prevent access to all mines and the smelter complex.
TCL sold 6,789 tonnes of copper and 12,142 tonnes of lead in the quarter to end-June.
Whyte said the lead smelter was also out of commission. The smelter was shut down before the strike action for upgrading.
"We had shut the lead smelter down, whether it was anticipating the strike or not, I can't give you the answer," he said.
Whyte said the company had been in contact with its clients over supplies. "We have been in touch with our clients and the necessary arrangements have been made."
Strikers last Friday took control of certain key areas of TCL, including the copper smelter and Kombat property.
The company obtained an urgent interim court interdict last Thursday declaring the strike unlawful but Namibian police have found it difficult to enforce the court order.
